item: The scaling benchmark's corpus context counts keyword_mentions with count(1), so the 300 s per-member deadline the diagnostics bundle puts around benchmark.json can stop it (a bare count(*) is one VM opcode the deadline's progress handler is never asked inside); the sweep that said that block had no deadline was wrong, and says so
refs: PR #1563; audit 0.5.0; R309; deadline-bound sweep S6
summary: RC2 found, while building its S3 test for performance.py, that benchmark.py's _store_and_corpus (called by run_benchmark, which is the benchmark.json member of the all-diagnostics bundle) counted keyword_mentions with a bare count(*) inside the bundle's per-member statement_deadline (bundle.py, the block around every database-touching member, 300 s by default). The WAL lane's deadline-bound sweep had noted this statement with the words 'no deadline around it'; that was wrong for the bundle path, and the sweep file now says so: the recording never ran the bundle's members, only the test suite's shapes, and a call site's wrapper is a fact about its CALLER. A bare count(*) is one OP_Count opcode, so the handler (asked once per 20,000 opcodes) cannot stop it; count(1) loops (about three opcodes per row). The corpus context now reads session.execute(text('SELECT count(1) FROM keyword_mentions')).scalar() or 0, the same number. tests/test_benchmark_corpus_count_deadline.py (5 tests): the shipped function under the REAL deadline at 1e-6 over 30,000 mentions raises StatementTimeout (checked red against the statement respelled as a bare count(*)), and the four corpus counts equal what the tables hold on 0, 1, 1,000 and 30,000 mentions. A second recorder run over the whole bundle on a 15 MiB store (all 57 members, 32 of them database-touching, 28 of those with recorded statements, 671 distinct (member, statement) shapes) shows benchmark.json with count(1). Price: the same CPU the S1 and S2 rows record (the loop form costs about 44 ms per 1.24 M mentions warm); nothing was measured on the benchmark's own count above this size.
